nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration fees / sandbox testing costs

assumptions: The rate card provided is a PLACEHOLDER: all team members are currently generic 'Team member' resources at 75 USD/hour with only 1 FTE available in total. Actual costs will change materially once real roles (e.g. backend/frontend engineer, QA, DevOps, PM) and their specific hourly rates are assigned — this estimate should be treated as indicative only.

Only 1 FTE is available against a 24-item, ~211-story-point backlog. At a conventional planning assumption of ~8 hours per story point (a common rough heuristic absent team velocity data), the raw effort implied is roughly 1,688 hours; we have added ~35% for integration, review, testing, deployment and coordination overhead (no other roles like QA/PM exist to absorb this), bringing total labour to 2,320 hours (~1.4 person-years for a single FTE working full time). This means the single 'Team member' role is staffed far too thinly for this backlog — either headcount must increase or scope/timeline must be reduced.

No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; this estimate is built from backlog points and generic effort heuristics only, not from observed team throughput or past project costs.

Story points were converted to hours using a flat multiplier per point, then weighted slightly upward for higher-priority/higher-complexity items (e.g. PW-8 legacy migration, PW-7 payment integration, PW-4 RBAC) since these typically carry hidden integration and data-quality risk.
Non-labour costs are indicative placeholders for third-party services (Stripe fees/sandbox, Oracle migration tooling, accessibility audit) since no vendor quotes were supplied.

Scenario spread (Optimistic/Most Likely/Pessimistic) reflects uncertainty inherent in a single-resource plan and unestimated integration/testing risk, especially around PW-7 (payments), PW-8 (legacy migration), and PW-14 (multi-currency).
Priority breakdown totals are derived by allocating each task's estimated cost (points-weighted share of total labour + associated non-labour) into its stated priority bucket.

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 (Admin back-office), PW-19 (Usage analytics), PW-23 (Contract tests) and PW-24 (Decommission legacy portal) — all Low priority — to a later phase.
reductions.effect: Removes ~300 hours of low-priority backlog (points: 13+8+5+8=34) from the initial delivery, deferring roughly 22,500 USD of labour cost to a future phase.

reductions.description: Reduce scope of PW-14 Multi-currency support to a single settlement currency (display-only FX for others) for MVP.
reductions.effect: Cuts estimated effort on this 13-point item by roughly half (~100 hours), deferring full multi-currency settlement to a later release.

reductions.description: Defer PW-15 Accessibility WCAG 2.2 AA pass and its associated third-party audit until post-launch hardening phase.
reductions.effect: Removes ~90 hours of labour plus the 1,500 USD external audit cost from the initial estimate; accessibility work is still recommended before general public launch.

reductions.description: Increase team capacity beyond the current 1 FTE placeholder rather than stretching a single resource across all 24 items, converting overtime/context-switching overhead into planned parallel work.
reductions.effect: Adding a second FTE at the same placeholder rate reduces calendar time and the ~35% coordination/rework overhead applied for a single-person team, potentially saving ~200 hours of inefficiency-driven cost once real roles and rates are set.

input.reasoning: With only a placeholder rate card (single 'Team member' role at 75 USD/hour, 1 FTE), I treated the entire 24-item backlog as work for that one role. I estimated effort using story points as a rough size proxy: totaling the 24 backlog items gives 211 points. Using an approximate 8 hours/point baseline (a common rough default for small-to-medium features), that's ~1,688 hours of raw feature work. Because there is no separate QA, DevOps, or PM role staffed, I added ~35% overhead for pipeline setup (PW-1 is a blocking prerequisite), integration testing, bug-fixing, deployment and coordination that a real team would normally split across specialist roles — bringing total labour to 2,320 hours (~174,000 USD at 75 USD/hour). I flagged this explicitly as a thin-staffing risk: 1 FTE cannot realistically deliver ~2,320 hours (1.4 person-years) in a normal project timeframe without either extending the schedule substantially or increasing headcount. Non-labour costs (Stripe fees, Oracle migration tooling, accessibility audit) were added as small indicative placeholders given no vendor quotes exist. I built three scenarios: Optimistic equal to the raw line-item total (178,000 USD, assuming everything goes as planned), Most Likely adding ~14.6% for typical rework/scope clarification (204,000 USD), and Pessimistic adding ~39% for high-risk items like legacy data migration, payment integration, and multi-currency support going over (248,000 USD). Priority breakdown apportions cost by each task's share of total story points within its priority bucket. Cost-reduction recommendations focus on descoping/deferring Low-priority items, trimming Multi-currency and Accessibility scope for MVP, and rethinking the single-FTE staffing model, which is the single biggest cost and schedule risk in this estimate."}
